items.title: An elapsed timer the OS ticks for you
items.description: notificationStartedAt + notificationShowTimer put a running clock in the Android tracking notification, and startedAt + showTimer do the same for an iOS Live Activity. The system advances both — no reposts, so no once-a-minute rewrite of your own and no alert on each one. notificationOnlyAlertOnce covers the other half: notification text that changes while tracking runs can now update silently.

items.title: showNotificationOnPauseOnly no longer defeats stopOnTerminate
items.description: Hiding the notification demotes the foreground service, and Android kills a process holding none when its task is removed — so a swipe from recents in that window took the process with it. The setting is now ignored while stopOnTerminate is false, and says so once in the log. getForegroundServiceHealth() reports a hidden-on-purpose notification as a fourth result, suppressed, instead of claiming a service that is not there.

items.title: Events keep reaching your headless task
items.description: With another plugin's background engine in the app — firebase_messaging's, typically — task removal could leave Tracelet broadcasting into an event fan-out with no members at all. Native tracking ran on and Dart received nothing, silently. Events now fall through to the registered headless task whenever no engine can receive them.
